context:
Goal: the work goes on now, and you can overrule any coordinator pick.
Problem (goal): the coordinator took this undoable pick on Nov 12, 13:12 CST without asking you; it stands unless you choose b.
Based on (ruling): your ruling R53 (13:07 CST: CI and merge alarms wake the batch runner, no GitHub issue) and rule git-main-only-by-pr (main moves only by pull request), cited by the coordinator.
Departs from: main has no such pick on record — the work it governs follows this pick.

options.gain: An alarm on main reaches the batch runner through the pull request that made that commit, with no new channel to build.
options.how: The cap alarm on main posts a comment on the merged pull request behind the run's commit; the comment carries the run id, so a run already alarmed is skipped. A commit with no pull request ends the alarm job red with the reason in its summary. The batch runner stays subscribed to a merged pull request until main's run on it ends. Undo: revert the commit.
options.label: Keep the pick (Recommended)
options.lose: A commit pushed to main without a pull request alarms only as a red job, not a wake.

options.gain: Every main run can wake the runner, pull request or not.
options.how: Build a separate wake channel for main runs that does not depend on a pull request.
options.label: Overrule it
options.lose: A new channel to build and keep, and the cap alarm waits for it.

reply: Filed: the pick stands. A CI alarm on main wakes the batch runner through a comment on the merged pull request behind it.
short: Main alarm wakes via the merged PR
title: A CI alarm on main wakes the batch runner through the merged pull request behind it
why: A coordinator pick you could not see before.
